o1.biggest_strength: Puts the code and one matched product in the very first email, then gives the sunscreen its own email with the real review line answering the white-cast fear that explains its 2.2% order rate.
o1.biggest_mistake: Leaves a hole in the exit rule: a buyer who orders on a marketplace never shows as 'Placed Order' in Klaviyo and will keep getting the series, and no email states what the 10% is actually worth on a typical ₹699 order.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add the marketplace-buyer treatment and a price line like '₹70 off a typical order', and put the active and strength into more subject lines.

o2.biggest_strength: Spots the marketplace tracking gap, telling past marketplace buyers to ignore the email, and writes full three-way quiz versions with correct discounted prices (₹359, ₹1,167).
o2.biggest_mistake: Contradicts itself on sensitive skin: Email 2 tells the dry/sensitive group not to start with an acid, then Email 5 gives everyone a salicylic acid face wash morning and night while also saying to use actives every other day first.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Remove the invented 14-day code expiry and its 'ends in 3 days/tomorrow' urgency, and make the Email 5 routine actually respect the sensitive-skin branch.

reason: Output 1 is the one I could hand to my team tomorrow — it leads with the code and a matched product, answers the sunscreen doubts and stays consistent — while Output 2 makes me fix a contradiction that would send my sensitive-skin customers a salicylic acid wash twice a day and builds urgency on a code deadline I never set.
